uncertain.note: the glyph after 'mes' is an italic long s, read as the marker {ſ} keying the first margin note (it slopes and descends, unlike the roman ſ of 'meſme' beside it); a reader could instead take it as part of the word. 'mes' completes a word broken at the foot of the previous page.

uncertain.note: 'anciẽs' and 'biẽ' carry a mark over the e that I read as a tilde (same shape as the tilde over o in 'demõſtroyent'); it could be read as an acute. 'biẽ aux' is set very tight, nearly touching.

uncertain.note: the print sets a space before each comma ('nu , de tant ... promptement , &'); normalized away as compositor spacing per §1.
the free-standing 'x' before 'c.v.' is legible but makes no obvious sense in the citation; transcribed as printed.

first character is a plain upright italic stroke with serifs: read as 'I', but it is very likely 'l' (lex) — the italic l elsewhere on the page has a looped ascender. The mark after it reads as a comma but could be a period.
a small dash/hyphen is printed immediately before the key letter y at the start of this note ('-y L. i.parag.'); it is not part of the note's text and may be a stray sort or damaged rule.
the final numeral shows three minims (i-i-j) at the highest magnification available, so 'iij'; at reading size it can look like 'ij'.
the abbreviation for the Digest is printed as a swash italic capital D; transcribed as plain 'D'. 'rit.' has the curled italic t.
